memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Put the atonement cover on the ark of the covenant law in the Most Holy Place. Place the table outside the curtain on the north side of the tabernacle and put the lampstand opposite it on the south side." - Exodus 26:34-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God assigns each piece its place: the atonement cover on the ark in the Most Holy Place, the table on the north side, the lampstand opposite on the south. Nothing is positioned randomly. Every item has a location, and the arrangement itself is part of God's design.

There is a principle here that runs right through Scripture. Our God is a God of order, not confusion (1 Cor 14:33). He brought order out of chaos at creation, and He builds order into how His people worship and live. This is not cold bureaucracy; it is the care of a God who wants things to function well and beautifully.

That has gentle implications for us. Order in our lives — how we use our time, arrange our priorities, structure our days — is not unspiritual. A life where everything is scattered and nothing has its place tends to crowd out the very things that matter most. God is not asking for rigid perfectionism, but He does invite us to put things in their proper order, with Him first. When our priorities sit where they belong, everything else finds its right proportion. What in your life is currently out of place?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Are the priorities of my life arranged in the order God intends?
What has crept into a place that belongs to something more important?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are a God of order and not confusion. Help me arrange my life with You in first place, so that everything else falls into its proper proportion. Amen.
